Fits: ZeroOneBeta iid intercept (1 | id) with sd(id) ~ z; ZeroOneBeta (0 + x | id) with sd(id, coef='x') ~ z; ZIP (0 + x | id), zi ~ 1, sd(id, dpar='mu', coef='x') ~ z. Agreement 1.9e-11 or better on 13 fits (3 ordinary seeds per route, plus 2 boundary-heavy seeds per ZeroOneBeta route with more than 40 percent exact 0 or 1 asserted), tolerance 1e-6, tightened from 1e-4 because the earlier quadrature passes at 1e-4 but fails at 1e-6; the verifier reports 13 expectations fail on e7dbc3f79, so the test discriminates the fix. Emulated bugs all above 20 x tol: reversed SD vector 5.9 to 25, SD intercept +log 2 8.8 to 14, sign-flipped SD slope 12 to 49, wrong group predictor 2.3 to 24, slope read as intercept 40 to 4779, atoms swapped 0.019 to 54 (smallest, ZOB slope seed 20261402, 19,000 x tol), zi halved 5.7 to 8. Console log clean (106 passed, 0 failures, errors, skips; the summary line omits the warnings field but no warning text appears). Slope-only scope: the two slope rows are supported for the slope-member SD only, because the fits are (0 + x | id) with no companion intercept field; this follows the lane rule that an unlabelled structured (1 + x | id) is two independent fields. What this does NOT establish: the boundary-heavy ZeroOneBeta slope seeds 20261409 and 20261412 were excluded after Julia raised 'matrix contains Infs or NaNs' in its SE Hessian on an interior response near 1e-56, so the boundary-heavy slope claim covers only the two seeds that fit (a post hoc choice), and this Julia failure is not yet in known-limitations.md. ZIP has no boundary-heavy draw and only zi ~ 1. A few seeds per route; no calibration, coverage, SE or Hessian parity, or recovery; no claim for any other family's iid route; fitted()/residuals() not covered. The oracle is accurate at these fixtures; it does not show the quadrature is accurate for larger SDs or other designs.
